\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{في} \ar{هذه} \ar{الأثناء} (fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ)}{في هذه الأثناء (fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ)}]{\ar{في} \ar{هذه} \ar{الأثناء} (fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ) — meanwhile, in the meantime}

\label{lesson:AR-C299-fi-hadhihi-al-athna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to burn down, then the Arabic for a firefighter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{في} \ar{هذه} \ar{الأثناء}}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{هذه} \ar{الأثناء}} — \emph{fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ} — \textquotedblleft{}meanwhile, in the meantime\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{في} \ar{هذه} \ar{الأثناء} \ar{كان} \ar{أخي} \ar{ينتظر} \ar{في} \ar{السيارة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ kāna akhī yantaẓiru fī as-sayyāra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Meanwhile my brother was waiting in the car.
\end{quote}

With \ar{كان} and the present it sets a second scene beside the first.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{هذه} \ar{الأثناء}} (\emph{fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ}) is \textquotedblleft{}in these folds\textquotedblright{}: \emph{athnāʾ} is a plural built on the native Arabic root \emph{th-n-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to fold, to double\textquotedblright{} (Lane), the root of \emph{ithnān}, two.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ kāna akhī yantaẓiru fī as-sayyāra.} — Meanwhile my brother was waiting in the car.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to burn down, then the Arabic for a firefighter, then say \emph{fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{في} \ar{هذه} \ar{الأثناء} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Meanwhile, in the meantime\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فيما} \ar{بعد} (fīmā baʿd)}{فيما بعد (fīmā baʿd)}]{\ar{فيما} \ar{بعد} (fīmā baʿd) — later on, afterwards}

\label{lesson:AR-C299-fima-bad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a firefighter, then the Arabic for meanwhile.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فيما} \ar{بعد}}
\textbf{\ar{فيما} \ar{بعد}} — \emph{fīmā baʿd} — \textquotedblleft{}later on, afterwards\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عرفت} \ar{السبب} \ar{فيما} \ar{بعد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿaraftu as-sabab fīmā baʿd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I found out the reason later on.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فيما} \ar{بعد}} (\emph{fīmā baʿd}) is \emph{fī}, \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{}, \emph{mā}, \textquotedblleft{}what\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{baʿd}, \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{}, which is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-ʿ-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to be far\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fīmā baʿd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fīmā baʿd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿaraftu as-sabab fīmā baʿd.} — I found out the reason later on.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a firefighter, then the Arabic for meanwhile, then say \emph{fīmā baʿd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{فيما} \ar{بعد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Later on, afterwards\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{في} \ar{اليوم} \ar{التالي} (fī al-yawm at-tālī)}{في اليوم التالي (fī al-yawm at-tālī)}]{\ar{في} \ar{اليوم} \ar{التالي} (fī al-yawm at-tālī) — the next day}

\label{lesson:AR-C299-fi-al-yawm-at-tali}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for meanwhile, then the Arabic for later on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{في} \ar{اليوم} \ar{التالي}}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{اليوم} \ar{التالي}} — \emph{fī al-yawm at-tālī} — \textquotedblleft{}the next day\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{في} \ar{اليوم} \ar{التالي} \ar{عاد} \ar{المسافر} \ar{إلى} \ar{بيته}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fī al-yawm at-tālī ʿāda al-musāfir ilā baytihi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The next day the traveller went back home.
\end{quote}

At night: \ar{في} \ar{الليلة} \ar{التالية}, the following night.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{اليوم} \ar{التالي}} (\emph{fī al-yawm at-tālī}) is \textquotedblleft{}on the following day\textquotedblright{}: \emph{tālī} is the participle of \emph{talā}, \textquotedblleft{}to follow\textquotedblright{}, built on the native Arabic root \emph{t-l-w} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī al-yawm at-tālī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī al-yawm at-tālī ʿāda al-musāfir ilā baytihi.} — The next day the traveller went back home.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for meanwhile, then the Arabic for later on, then say \emph{fī al-yawm at-tālī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ذكر} (dhakara)}{ذكر (dhakara)}]{\ar{ذكر} (dhakara) — to mention; to remember}

\label{lesson:AR-C299-dhakara-mention}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for later on, then the Arabic for the next day.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ذكر}}
\textbf{\ar{ذكر}} — \emph{dhakara} — \textquotedblleft{}to mention; to remember\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ذكر} \ar{المراسل} \ar{اسم} \ar{القرية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dhakara al-murāsil ism al-qarya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The correspondent mentioned the name of the village.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يذكر}, \emph{yadhkur}.

The taught \ar{ذكرى}, a memory, is the same root.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ذكر}} (\emph{dhakara}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{dh-k-r}, which joins keeping a thing in mind and saying it aloud: \emph{dhikrā}, a memory, and \emph{tadhakkara}, to recall, share it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhakara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhakara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhakara al-murāsil ism al-qarya.} — The correspondent mentioned the name of the village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for later on, then the Arabic for the next day, then say \emph{dhakara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ذكر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To mention; to remember\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نقل} (naqala)}{نقل (naqala)}]{\ar{نقل} (naqala) — to pass on, to report; to carry}

\label{lesson:AR-C299-naqala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for the next day, then the Arabic for to mention.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نقل}}
\textbf{\ar{نقل}} — \emph{naqala} — \textquotedblleft{}to pass on, to report; to carry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نقلت} \ar{الصحيفة} \ar{كلام} \ar{المدير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{naqalat aṣ-ṣaḥīfa kalām al-mudīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The newspaper reported what the manager said.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينقل}, \emph{yanqul}.

It also moves people and goods: \ar{نقل} \ar{الأثاث}, to move the furniture.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نقل}} (\emph{naqala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-q-l} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to move a thing from one place to another\textquotedblright{}. Words moved from one mouth to another are reported.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naqala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naqala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naqalat aṣ-ṣaḥīfa kalām al-mudīr.} — The newspaper reported what the manager said.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for the next day, then the Arabic for to mention, then say \emph{naqala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نقل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pass on, to report; to carry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
